'''Gianni De Michelis''' (26 November 1940 – 11 May 2019) was an Italian politician and a member of the [[Italian Socialist Party]] (PSI), who served as minister in many Italian governments in the 1980s and early 1990s.<ref>{{Cite web|language=it
|url=https://www.repubblica.it/politica/2019/05/11/news/addio_a_de_michelis_protagonista_della_prima_repubblica-225989895/|title=Addio a De Michelis, protagonista della Prima Repubblica|date=May 11, 2019|website=la Repubblica}}</ref>

==Biography==
De Michelis was born in [[Venice]] in 1940.<ref name="wpforum" /> He graduated in 1963 in Industrial Chemistry at the [[University of Padua]] and began his academic career, first as an assistant and then as a lecturer, becoming an associate professor of Chemistry in 1980 at the [[Ca' Foscari University of Venice]]. After a long leave due to political and institutional commitments, he returned to university teaching from 1994 to 1999.

He started his political career with the Italian Socialist Party, where he was elected to the municipal council of Venice. He got elected for the first time to the [[Italian Parliament]] in 1976 and was elected again in 1979, 1983, 1987, 1992 and 2006. He was Minister of State Holdings from 1980 to 1983. He then became Minister of Work in 1986 (with [[Bettino Craxi]] as President of the Council). However, he reached the peak of his political career with his nomination to the Vice-Presidency of the Council in 1988-1989. He became Minister for Foreign Affairs in 1989 and kept that post until 1992.

Between 1993 and 2001, during the so-called "judicial storm of [[Mani Pulite]]", he was accused of corruption along with many of the socialist MPs and regional administrators. Within more than 35 different trails, apart from the numerous favorable verdicts, he was convicted of [[political corruption|corruption]] and sentenced to 1 year and 6 months (negotiated) in [[Venice]] for highways bribes in [[Veneto]] and to 6 months for illegal financing ([[Enimont bribe]], also negotiated).

In 1996, De Michelis founded a political movement named the [[Socialist Party (Italy, 1996)|Socialist Party]] with [[Ugo Intini]] and other former [[Italian Socialist Party]] (PSI) members, which later was joined by the [[Socialist League (Italy)|Socialist League]] of [[Claudio Martelli]] and [[Bobo Craxi]] to form the [[New Italian Socialist Party|New PSI]] in 2001. He was elected secretary of the new party at the first congress.

De Michelis was elected at the [[2004 European Parliament election in Italy|2004 European elections]] as a [[Member of the European Parliament]] (MEP) for Southern Italy with the NPSI, and was therefore a [[Non-Inscrits|Non-Inscrit]] in the [[European Parliament]] whilst awaiting the acceptance of his party's request of membership in the [[Progressive Alliance of Socialists and Democrats|Socialist Group]]. He sat in the [[Committee on Industry, Research and Energy]], and was a substitute for the [[Committee on Legal Affairs]], a member of the Delegation for relations with the [[People's Republic of China]] and a substitute for the Delegation to the [[Parliamentary Assembly of the Union for the Mediterranean|Euro-Mediterranean Parliamentary Assembly]].

His leadership, however, had been contested in the Congress of October 2005, where the son of [[Bettino Craxi]], [[Bobo Craxi]], claimed to have been declared [[secretary]] after De Michelis had left the hall, declaring the Congress void. This led Bobo Craxi to open a judicial case. The judge, on the second verdict, unquestionably confirmed the right to use the symbol and the secretary to Gianni De Michelis.

At the [[2006 Italian general election]], he was elected MP for the Italian parliament but gave his seat to [[Lucio Barani]] since he decided to stay in the European Parliament. In October 2007, De Michelis joined the newly formed [[Italian Socialist Party (2007)|Socialist Party]], made up of the diaspora of the historical PSI. At this time, De Michelis, along with fellow former NPSI MEP [[Alessandro Battilocchio]], was admitted into the [[Political groups of the European Parliament|parliamentary group]] of the [[Party of European Socialists]].

De Michelis died in [[Venice]] on 11 May 2019 at the age of 78.<ref name=wpforum>{{cite web|title=Biographies|url=http://www.theworldpoliticalforum.net/wp-content/uploads/wpf2003/05_founding_conference_turin/varie/bio.pdf|publisher=The World Politics Forum |access-date=1 April 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714193451/http://www.theworldpoliticalforum.net/wp-content/uploads/wpf2003/05_founding_conference_turin/varie/bio.pdf|archive-date=14 July 2014 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/cronaca/2019/05/11/e-morto-gianni-de-michelis_564f655c-b68e-43c3-9a59-05dddf3f42c7.html|title=E' morto Gianni De Michelis, ex ministro del Psi di Craxi - Cronaca|date=May 11, 2019|website=Agenzia ANSA}}</ref>

==Personal life==
De Michelis was a great lover of dance and discos. In 1988, he wrote a book entitled "''Dove Andiamo a Ballare Questa Sera''?" ({{langx|en|Where to Go Dancing this Night?}}) in which he reviewed 250 Italian dance nightclubs.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://theintermediateperiod.wordpress.com/2017/10/28/gianni-de-michelis-dove-andiamo-a-ballare-questa-sera/|title=Gianni De Michelis' 'Dove andiamo a ballare questa sera?'|date=October 28, 2017}}</ref>
